# Node2Shell-CVE-2026-111497-POC

## Node.js Brotli Decoder Out-of-Bounds Write to Denial of Service / Remote Code Execution

---

## 1. Vulnerability Overview

**CVE ID:** CVE-2026-111497
**Name:** Node2Shell
**Severity:** Critical 9.2 (CVSS v4.0)
**Type:** Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) via unchecked return value (CWE-252)
**Component:** Node.js bundled Brotli decoder (`c/dec/decode.c`)

**Root Cause:** `DecodeBlockTypeAndLength()` returns `BROTLI_FALSE` (0) when `max_block_type <= 1`. But `BROTLI_FALSE == BROTLI_DECODER_SUCCESS == 0`. The streaming API's `BROTLI_SAFE` macro misreads this as "need more input", saving state at `BROTLI_STATE_COMMAND_BEGIN` with `block_length[1]` still 0. Every subsequent call hits the same state, creating a permanent `NEEDS_MORE_INPUT` loop (DoS). In the non-safe (batch) path, the return value is discarded, `block_length[1]` underflows to `UINT32_MAX`, and subsequent array accesses are out-of-bounds (OOB write).

**Impact:**
- DoS: Server hangs permanently (reliable, all unpatched versions)
- RCE: Code execution inside the Node.js process (with heap spray)
- Memory Disclosure: Leaked process memory

---

## 2. Affected Versions

| Software | Fixed Version |
|----------|---------------|
| Node.js 22.x | 22.23.4 |
| Node.js 24.x | 24.22.1 |
| Node.js 26.x | 26.12.1 |
| Node.js 20.x, 25.x | EOL, no fix (always vulnerable) |
| Bun | 1.4.4 |
| Brotli library | 1.0.10, 1.1.1, or 1.2.1 |

## 4. How the POC Works

### The Trigger

The 13-byte OOB write trigger (`900040040100400405010140 00`) constructs a Brotli bitstream (RFC 7932, LSB-first) that:

1. Declares `NBLTYPESI=2` (two insert-copy block types)
2. Sets IC block-length type-0 = 1 (decoder exhausts after 1 IC command)
3. Sets IC block-length type-1 = 0 (invalid)
4. After the first IC command, the decoder switches to block type 1
5. `DecodeBlockTypeAndLength(max_block_type=1)` returns `BROTLI_FALSE` (0)
6. Streaming API: misreads 0 as `NEEDS_MORE_INPUT`, saves state, loops forever (DoS)
7. Batch API: discards return, `block_length[1]` underflows to `UINT32_MAX` (OOB write)

The 8-byte DoS trigger (`4200800801002082`) is a truncated version that causes the streaming decoder to hang immediately.

### The Delivery

The exploit uses raw socket with chunked transfer encoding:
- Sends the trigger as a chunked HTTP POST body
- Does NOT send the terminating 0-length chunk
- The connection stays alive, keeping the decoder stuck
- Express 5 / body-parser 2.x decompresses the body with Node.js's Brotli decoder

### The Spray

For RCE, the 13-byte trigger is followed by a heap spray:
- The spray contains JS code (e.g., `require('child_process').exec(cmd)`)
- The OOB write corrupts decoder struct pointers
- On targets with ASLR disabled or known layout, the corrupted pointer calls the spray
- The embedded JS code executes with Node.js process permissions

### BrotliDecoderState Struct Layout

The OOB write targets specific fields in the decoder state struct:

| Offset | Field | Spray Index |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| 64 | buffer.u8[0] | spray[3] |
| 72 | buffer_length | spray[11] (OOB jump byte) |
| 128 | ringbuffer | spray[16] |
| 288 | block_length[1] | spray[176] |
| 720 | metadata_start_func | spray[608] |
| 728 | metadata_chunk_func | spray[616] |
| 736 | metadata_callback_opaque | spray[624] |

Formula: `spray[k]` maps to `struct_offset 112+k` for k >= 12 (after the 3-byte bit-reader pre-load shift).

# CVE-2026-58868 

Hey everyone, this is my first post, so if you spot any mistakes, please let me know. I don't usually write about my CVEs, but Harry Kane finally winning the Ballon d'Or felt like a good excuse to do something special. Before getting into the bug, here's how I ended up looking at Android in the first place.

Most of my time goes into watching football and researching Windows. One day, there were no matches to watch, and I was bored of staring at Windows disassembly. Then my old Oneplus android phone caught my eye, and I thought, might as well tinker with it.

I wasn't very familiar with Android, so I used an LLM to help me understand how things fit together. I ended up liking it for a pretty obvious reason: I could just read the source code. After poking around for a while, I found a zero click Dos bug in `system_server` involving mDNS.

That made me want to keep digging. Media parsers seemed like an interesting place to look, especially given how often they show up for zero click exploit. So I started reading the media code, with some help from AI to make sense of the unfamiliar parts. I found the bug through static analysis, which is how I do my Windows research.

## Summary

CVE-2026-58868 is an out-of-bounds write in Android's HEIF image-decoding path. A crafted image can make the decoder place tiles outside the allocated output image, causing `mediaserver` to write converted pixels out of bounds. Google classifies it as a **Critical RCE** affecting **Android 14, 15, 16, 16 QPR2, and 17**. ([Android bulletin](https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/2026/2026-11-01))
**But I have reproduced this also in an Android 12 device (moto g31).**

In Gmail, opening the email was enough: thumbnail generation decoded the image without me tapping it or manually downloading the attachment. I also reproduced the issue through Google Files and Google Photos. The crash below is from Gmail on my OnePlus  CPH2467.

## Root cause

A HEIF grid image is assembled from smaller encoded tiles. The output buffer is sized for the overall image, while decoded tile dimensions determine where each tile is placed. In the reproducer, the tiles decode to 1024 x 1024, but the declared output dimensions do not accommodate that tile layout.

[StagefrightMetadataRetriever](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/av/+/1863cb0ea5a9e1340f11a435618ff863e017da29/media/libmediaplayerservice/StagefrightMetadataRetriever.cpp#269) reads the tile dimensions and uses them to select a suitable codec:

```cpp
if (!thumbnail && isHeif && format != NULL) {
    int32_t tileWidth, tileHeight;
    if (trackMeta->findInt32(kKeyTileWidth, &tileWidth) && tileWidth > 0
            && trackMeta->findInt32(kKeyTileHeight, &tileHeight) && tileHeight > 0) {
        format->setInt32("height", tileHeight);
        format->setInt32("width", tileWidth);
    }
}
```

Here, `thumbnail` means a thumbnail stored inside the file; an app can generate its preview by decoding the main image.

The bug is in [`MediaImageDecoder::onOutputReceived()`](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/av/+/1863cb0ea5a9e1340f11a435618ff863e017da29/media/libstagefright/FrameDecoder.cpp#1036). It calculates each tile's destination using the decoded crop dimensions. It clips the right and bottom edges to the output size, but does not first reject a tile whose starting position is already outside the image. A tile starting below the canvas can therefore produce a negative crop height.

[ColorConverter](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/av/+/1863cb0ea5a9e1340f11a435618ff863e017da29/media/libstagefright/colorconversion/ColorConverter.cpp#660) checks that the source and destination crop dimensions agree:

```cpp
src.cropWidth() == dst.cropWidth() &&
src.cropHeight() == dst.cropHeight()
```

Both rectangles can be invalid in the same way and still pass these comparisons. The other stride and alignment checks do not establish that the complete rectangles are within bounds.

The [semiplanar conversion wrapper](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/av/+/1863cb0ea5a9e1340f11a435618ff863e017da29/media/libstagefright/colorconversion/ColorConverter.cpp#948) then passes the crop dimensions to libyuv. Abbreviating the chroma and matrix selection:

```cpp
libyuvFunc(src_y, src_stride_y, src_uv, src_stride_uv,
           dst_ptr, dst.mStride, matrix,
           src.cropWidth(), src.cropHeight());
```

libyuv takes the height as a signed integer. The dump is consistent with an invalid crop reaching this call as height `-1096`. In [`NV21ToARGBMatrix`](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/libyuv/+/0dbb8351b69b62539acfd5b05f5630fba662ad00/source/convert_argb.cc#4078), a negative height requests vertically inverted output, so libyuv adjusts the destination pointer before converting pixels. An invalid crop has now become a write outside the output buffer.
